transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-03
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~38 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Raj (QuantumLeaf CTO), Sofia (Product), Evan (DevOps)

Auto-generated Summary (may be rough): Quick discovery on PLG path, free credits, and how Redwood can get their teams to a first invocation in under an hour. Talked about hosted first, later dedicated/reserved or VPC for production. Security and audit asked by Raj.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, and with me is Liam our solutions engineer. How's it going over there?
[00:06] Raj: Hi Maya, hey Liam. Good to be here. I'm Raj, CTO at QuantumLeaf — we build assistant features into our analytics dashboard.
[00:11] Sofia: Sofia here, product. We're mainly trying to see how fast our devs can get a working prototype using your hosted API.
[00:16] Liam: Great, thanks. Quick agenda—today we'll qualify your stack, your timeline, what success looks like, and cover free credits and the zero-to-first-invocation path. Sound good?
[00:23] Raj: Yep. We're on a tight timeline — want to ship an internal prototype in three weeks. Ideally devs can try it locally and then move to a sandbox.
[00:31] Maya: Perfect, that's exactly the PLG path we optimize for. A few quick qual questions: current model usage, latency expectations, and any blockers like data residency or on-prem needs?
[00:41] Raj: Current: prototype with OpenModelX in-house, but ops cost is high. For latency, interactive UI target is ~200-300ms median per token ideally, but we'll accept higher in early stages. We do have a regulated customer in EU so data residency matters later.
[00:54] Evan: Also, we'll need SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration when we hit prod. For the prototype, we just need secure creds and minimal logging.
[01:03] Liam: Makes sense. For quickstarts, our hosted API is fastest: you sign up, we provision free credits, you use the REST/SDK, and your teams can hit first inference in minutes. If you need lower latency or more throughput later, we can talk Dedicated pools or Private VPC.
[01:18] Sofia: Can you walk through the exact steps a developer takes from signup to first call? We want to include that in our onboarding docs.
[01:25] Maya: Absolutely. Step 1: create an org and API key in the console. Step 2: SDK or curl examples — we've got templates for web and backend use. Step 3: sample prompt sets and a small eval harness we can pre-populate in your account. Step 4: run a small perf test — sample request/response to confirm latency. We also provide a one-click enable for streaming responses if you need them.
[01:45] Raj: How much effort from our side for telemetry and tracing? We want to correlate request ids with our front-end traces.
[01:52] Liam: We provide request-level IDs and tracing hooks you can pass through headers. The console shows per-route latency and token breakdown; you can export logs or stream to your SIEM.
[02:02] Sofia: About free credits — is that limited per org/user? Any time limits?
[02:07] Maya: We typically issue a sandbox credit package for PLG onramp—sized for a few thousand requests over 30 days. It's meant to get you to a prototype; after that we discuss usage plans or reserved capacity if you expect continuous traffic.
[02:19] Raj: For the EU-regulated customer, we will need data not to leave EU for production. Is that doable with Hosted?
[02:26] Liam: We have regional hosting in EU; for production with strict residency it's common to either use our EU-hosted instance or move to Redwood Private with a VPC or on-prem package for full control. The hosted EU cluster meets most residency needs, but for full customer audit/air-gap we recommend Private.
[02:42] Evan: On KMS: can we bring our own key?
[02:45] Liam: Yes, for Dedicated and Private you can bring your own KMS/HSM. Hosted supports envelope encryption and customer-managed keys for select enterprise tiers. We'll share the KMS integration guide.
[02:56] Raj: What about cost? We want a ballpark so product can plan.
[02:59] Maya: For hosted PLG credits it's usage-based per token. For pilots we can propose a pilot package with a blended rate; if you later move to Dedicated we do reserved capacity contracts. I'll include ballpark numbers in the SOW.
[03:12] Sofia: Performance—how do you handle KV cache and long conversations? Our use case keeps multi-turn context of ~2k tokens.
[03:20] Liam: Our runtime supports efficient KV cache and batching. For long contexts we'll recommend a model variant and possible quantization to keep latency down — caching reduces repeat token compute for prefix tokens. Apologies, sometimes the transcript shows K-V cash for KV cache—ignore that, ha.
[03:34] Raj: Haha, noted. Any blockers for us to try the sandbox today?
[03:38] Maya: No blockers. I can kick off credit provisioning after the call — we'll need an admin email to invite.
[03:44] Raj: That's me, raj@quantumleaf.com.
[03:47] Maya: Great, I'll send the invite and credits.
[03:50] Evan: For the benchmark, what do you need from us?
[03:53] Liam: Ideally a small representative prompt set (10-20 prompts), expected QPS, and target latency/cost. We'll run the benchmark on Hosted first and can run on Dedicated if you want reserved throughput.
[04:05] Raj: QPS for prototype is low — maybe 1-5 qps, but we want to know headroom.
[04:09] Sofia: Who are the stakeholders we should expect for security reviews later?
[04:12] Raj: It's me + our security lead (not on this call) + legal for contracts.
[04:18] Maya: Good to know. We'll add our security pack to the follow-up. It includes SOC2, data flow diagrams, and pen test summary.
[04:25] Raj: Any mention of competitors— we've looked at Anthropic and HostedCloudX. Why Redwood vs them?
[04:31] Liam: Two reasons: production-first controls (batching, caching, model routing) and unified experience across hosted/dedicated/private so you don't re-architect when you scale. Plus our console shows token-level cost so product can optimize.
[04:45] Sofia: Are there any rate limits in sandbox? We don't want throttling when a few devs test.
[04:50] Maya: Sandbox has modest rate limits to prevent abuse but we'll bump them for your team during pilot. For larger scale tests we'll move you to a dedicated test bucket.
[04:58] Evan: How do rollouts work—can we canary to a small percent?
[05:02] Liam: Yes, the console supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant if latency or errors spike.
[05:09] Raj: Ok — success criteria for pilot: 1) teams can go from signup to first working prototype within a day, 2) median latency < 400ms for initial model, 3) demo to internal stakeholders at week three. That's our rough bar.
[05:22] Maya: That's achievable. We'll tailor the free credits and sample prompts to help you reach that.
[05:27] Sofia: Any gotchas with SDKs — we use Node backend and React frontend.
[05:31] Liam: We have official SDKs for Node and Python and frontend examples for streaming in React. Most teams wire up auth header + streaming socket or SSE. We'll share quickstart snippets.
[05:41] Raj: About observability—how granular is the cost breakdown? Product wants to know which prompts are expensive.
[05:46] Liam: Token-level cost per request is shown in the console; you can tag requests and get per-route breakdowns. We also export usage CSVs for cost analysis.
[05:55] Sofia: For EU residency later, is there additional cost?
[05:58] Maya: Regional hosting may have slight pricing differences. If you move to Private/VPC there are platform fees for the private control plane. We'll outline options in the SOW.
[06:07] Evan: Anything on compliance for logs retention? Our legal needs 12 months of audit logs for one customer.
[06:12] Liam: We support configurable log retention for enterprise tiers. For Private you manage retention; for Hosted we can configure retention windows and provide exports for audit.
[06:21] Raj: Sounds good. Let's talk timeline: we'll try the sandbox this week, then schedule the perf check with Liam next week. If all good, legal starts contracting.
[06:29] Maya: Perfect. Quick note—we'll share an onboarding checklist: account creation, invite devs, import sample prompts, run benchmark. That should get you z2fi — zero-to-first-invocation — in under an hour for an experienced dev.
[06:43] Sofia: Nice term, we'll borrow that.
[06:46] Raj: Any final questions?
[06:48] Evan: One—are there examples of customers who moved from hosted trial to private for EU residency?
[06:54] Liam: Yes—several fintech and health customers start hosted then move to Private when residency and audit requirements tighten. We'll share an anonymized case study.
[07:05] Maya: Alright, I'll recap the next steps in email after this call. Thank you all for the time.
[07:11] Raj: Thanks everyone.
[07:13] Sofia: Thanks!
[07:14] Liam: Bye!

End of transcript.
